text:
### Observed differences

- In the later window, A32 and A33 almost disappear: A32 drops from about 53% of traces to 0.5%, and A33 from about 52.5% to 0.5%; their former successor patterns (A32→A28/A33, A33→A32/A28) are replaced by single rare edges to A44 and A24 respectively. [OCC004, OCC005, DIR004, DIR005, REL026, POS002, POS003]
- A27 becomes near-universal, rising from about 48% of traces to 100%, and it is followed by A28 in almost all cases (about 98% before, 99.5% after). [OCC003, DIR003, REL020]
- A06 appears more often and earlier: its trace participation rises from about 7% to 29%, its position distribution becomes more concentrated (upper quartile moves from about 0.96 to 0.45), and it is more often placed immediately before A19, A26 or A28, and after A14 or A40. [OCC002, POS001, DIR001, REL001, REL002, REL004, REL007, LAG001, LAG002, LAG004]
- A14, A26 and A19 become more tightly coupled to A27: A14 before A27 rises from about 48% to 99%, A26 before A27 from 48% to 99.5%, A19 before A27 from 21% to 53.5%, and A26’s successor share to A27 rises from about 47% to 98%. [REL011, REL017, REL014, DIR002, LAG006]
- A02 decreases from about 11% of traces to 2%. [OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in which the later window largely removes A32 and A33 from the main flow, makes A27 followed by A28 a near-universal step, and adds or expands A06 as an additional step that occurs before A27/A28 and after A14/A40. The change is directly visible in occurrence, successor, relative-order and lag indicators, and the number of qualifying items (53) far exceeds the 0.75 expected by chance. A competing explanation that the differences are only sampling variation in variant frequencies is unlikely given the consistency across many indicators, although the exact replacement edges for A32 and A33 rest on only one trace each. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR002, DIR003, REL011, REL017, REL020, LAG006]
